title: Martyr Fidelity and the Ideal Nihang

blocks.text: The page continues a martyrdom-inflected dialogue about the head, uncut hair, and the refusal to yield Sikh identity under coercion. It treats bodily suffering as secondary to keeping faith, so outward signs become part of an inward covenant rather than mere custom.

From that debate the text broadens into a warrior ideal, praising the ideal nihang as fearless in battle and first to step forward wherever the Panth is endangered. Courage, austerity, and readiness for sudden combat are all folded into the same religious temperament.

The effect is to join martyrdom and militancy instead of separating them. The Sikh warrior is admirable not because he loves violence, but because he has already accepted loss and therefore cannot be frightened away from duty.
